I had a class in college called "problem solving with computers" where they attempted to teach us mechanical engineers how to code in VBA. Our professor was a chemical engineer who barely knew the english language or the programming language. It was predictably disastrous. Anyway, one day we learned how to make message boxes. This came shortly after we learned how to make a Do loop. I wrote the following:

Sub legit()

box1:
 If MsgBox("Error: Too Legit", vbOKCancel, "Error") = vbOK Then GoTo box1
 
Do While True

 dummy = MsgBox("Error: Too Legit To Quit", vbOKCancel)
 
Loop

End Sub

I think at some point I made a custom message box that said "quit" instead of "cancel". I also eventually figured out how to get it to stop without force-quitting excel. It was fun for a while though.

In 1999 I not only fixed the Y2K problem for the law firm I worked for, I made a ASP web based Docket Calendar for them. I think it was one of the first web based docket calendars and it used Dynamic HTML JavaScript which later on got named Ajax. For Lawnet 2000 it won awards and was called commercial quality, and we built a practice area information system around it with other apps.

I got stressed out and in 2001 I developed a mental illness and got fired. But for me that Docket Calendar was the best thing I ever wrote, even if I never got credit for it and nobody knows who I am. Due to the employment contract my name was not put on the patents and they used manage names instead. But they licensed out the docket calendar to other law firms and courts.

Two years ago, I was still on Windows and still played Minecraft. My copy of Minecraft was pirated. I didn't use a pirated launcher since I found out the only one (at the time) was a Trojan. But Minecraft has an offline play mode, and if you logged in successfully, the game made an authentication file on your AppData folder which certified the launcher that you were able to login and therefore, could play offline. I then used the Trojan launcher on a Virtual Machine, brought the authentication file to my machine, blocked their servers on my hosts file and used the official launcher.

However, with this trick, I couldn't update the game. So, I figured out how to grab the game files from the server and made a little tool in C# for me and my friends which updated the game. Stupid, but I was really proud of it.

I wrote an AHK script that completed most of the game Zork by itself; you just clicked in the game window and ran the script, and it would do the rest.

Now of course Zork has many areas (namely fights) where there's an element of randomness...this was circumvented by repeating the relevant commands dozens of times (i.e. where a human would say "attack troll" five times and then see the troll die, the script will say "attack troll" fifty times before moving on because there's no way to know if it's dead or not).

There were a couple puzzles that just couldn't be solved using stone-written scripts, though, and I never finished it, but I got pretty damn far.
